articles.title: Zinedine Zidane waited for France - now what will he bring to role?
articles.summary: Zinedine Zidane says he waited for the France job, but what will he bring to the role after five years out of management?
articles.body:
France will have a new face on the touchline for the first time in 14 years when they face Turkey on Friday.

Zinedine Zidane replaced Didier Deschamps after France's fourth-place finish at the World Cup, but his appointment had been an open secret long before Les Bleus' third-place play-off loss to England.

Talks between the former Real Madrid manager and the French football authorities kicked off as early as February 2025 - after Zidane's former team-mate Deschamps announced a few weeks earlier he would step down following the 2026 World Cup.

When he was unveiled in Paris, Zidane was keen to highlight the time he had spent waiting on the sidelines and preparing for the job.

"I had several offers in the last four or five years, but I turned them all down," an emotional Zidane said. "The national team is the only thing I wanted."

While his enthusiasm at taking the job was the overarching theme of his first news conference in the French capital, the midfield legend offered few clues to France fans as to how he would approach the role.

Even a question on Kylian Mbappe's captaincy was bypassed: "The most important thing for him now is to rest, we'll have the chance to speak in September."

Mbappe, speaking to Spanish newspaper AS, has since said having the former Real Madrid star as his national team coach was "like a film".

When asked about his preferred style of play, Zidane opted against going into tactical detail.

"I can't explain to you in just a couple of words how we're going win. I have to arrive, meet with the players, and explain my plans to them. After that, it'll be up to me to keep this team winning."

However, Zidane confirmed his intention "to do things differently" and he has called up five uncapped players for this international break.

He went on to signal that there would be a degree of "continuation" from the work of his predecessor, which he made sure to praise.

"I'm going to try do what I know how to, but it won't be a complete break either."

So what will Zidane bring to the France dugout?

Zidane, who retired in 2006, was one of the most exciting attacking midfielders of his generation.

He won league titles and European trophies with Juventus and Real Madrid, while he helped France to victory at the 1998 World Cup and Euro 2000.

Zidane started his career at Cannes and then moved to Bordeuax.

He almost joined Premier League side Blackburn Rovers in 1995, but the move broke down with Rovers owner Jack Walker reportedly asking manager Kenny Dalglish: "Why do you want to sign Zidane when we have Tim Sherwood?"

Instead Zidane moved to Juventus, winning six trophies, before he was signed by Real Madrid for a then record £45.8m.

For France he was the hero of the home 1998 World Cup, scoring twice in the final, a 3-0 win over Brazil and was named the best player at Euro 2000.

He retired after the 2006 World Cup, a campaign full of highs, leading France to the final, and one big low, when his playing career ended after he was sent off in the showpiece match for headbutting Italy defender Marco Materazzi.

Zidane and Deschamps - two 1998 World Cup winners - do share a few similar traits in their management, not least in their pragmatism, as well as the laissez-faire approach to attacking phases which Deschamps embraced in the recent World Cup.

Given the attacking talent at his disposal, it stands to reason that Zidane would carry on in that vein.

"I was a number 10 as a player," he said, hinting he would retain the role Michael Olise thrived in for much of the summer.

"What motivates me is the game, it's scoring goals," he added.

With the team netting 20 times in North America, Deschamps has arguably laid the foundations for his successor's attacking set-up.

Zidane is finding Les Bleus in immeasurably better shape than his predecessor did at the start of his own tenure, at which point the wounds of the 2010 World Cup fiasco were still fresh.

The appointment does come with a degree of uncertainty, though.

Given that Zidane has spent five years out of management, and the Real Madrid job is the only other senior coaching role of his career, it might seem like a gamble.

The 54-year-old himself has acknowledged leading a national team would be an entirely new proposition: "It's new to me, but I'm not scared. This is what I wanted."

Predictably, the reaction among players and fans to Zidane's arrival has been almost unanimously positive. He was met with a crowd of supporters carrying flares and banners as he left the French Football Federation's headquarters after his unveiling.

"Welcome home," Mbappe wrote on Instagram later in the day.

"It's a great day for French football," his former France and Bordeaux team-mate Bixente Lizarazu told France Info later that day.

"He is more than fit to manage Les Bleus, given what he did at Real Madrid with great players and big egos."

The respect that the former Ballon d'Or winner commands in a dressing room is one of his key strengths.

Even more so than Deschamps, a France legend in his own right, Zidane is a figure who can rival - perhaps even overshadow - his own players in terms of star power.

In this sense, he may be the ideal manager to get the most out of an attack made up of Mbappe, Ousmane Dembele, Desire Doue and Olise.

This international break - lasting four Nations League fixtures over three weeks - will offer the France players a crash-course to the new management style.

After facing Turkey, they have two games against Belgium and one against Italy in Paris.

Given his iconic status within French football and on the wider national stage, Zidane will invariably enjoy an unprecedented degree of goodwill regardless of his initial results.

Whether he uses that leeway to experiment tactically and bring in new faces remains to be seen.

His homecoming at the Stade de France on Friday, 2 October, against the Azzurri no less, is an ideal fixture to begin the new era.

A version of this article was first published on 28 July.

articles.title: El hijo del mítico Roger Milla juega en Segunda con el filial del Celta
articles.standfirst: El histórico delantero que disputó tres Mundiales con Camerún, entre ellos España'82 (uno de los partidos en Balaídos), es el padre de Germain, jugador del Celta Fortuna
articles.summary: El histórico delantero que disputó tres Mundiales con Camerún, entre ellos España'82 (uno de los partidos en Balaídos), es el padre de Germain, jugador del Celta Fortuna
articles.body: "Antes no teníamos academias, teníamos sólo un entrenador. No había nada como esto”. A Roger le sorprendieron las instalaciones en las que iba a formarse como futbolista su hijo Germain, una vez cerrada en 2022, a través del convenio que se mantenía con el Fursan Hispania, club de Dubái fundado precisamente por Míchel Salgado, su incorporación a la cantera del Celta. Roger y Germain comparten el apellido Milla, lo que remite, en el caso del primero, al Mundial de 1982, 44 años han pasado, primero de los tres que, junto a los de Italia’90 y Estados Unidos’94, jugó con Camerún. Aquella selección dejó una huella imborrable en la cita de nuestro país, no perdiendo un solo partido, por más que cayera eliminada, en el grupo que compartía con Polonia, Perú e Italia. Precisamente el tercer y último duelo, frente a la selección transalpina, posterior campeona, se disputó en Vigo, en el estadio de Balaídos, con Milla asistiendo a M’Bida en la diana de los Leones Indomables. Roger, cuyo legado fue homenajeado por la propia FIFA en otro Mundial, el de Qatar, puede presumir sin duda de haber sido uno de los mejores futbolistas africanos de todos los tiempos, haciendo carrera sobre todo en el fútbol francés, tras pasar por Mónaco, Saint Etienne o Montpellier, y ganando además dos Copas de África con su combinado nacional. De tal palo, como suele suceder, tal astilla... Porque Germain, a sus 20 años, ya ha llegado al fútbol profesional después del ascenso a Segunda de un filial, el olívico, al que se había incorporado finalizada la campaña 24-25 y después de renovar contrato por cuatro temporadas. Suele desempeñarse por banda, con tendencia a ganar metros más allá de que la propia web del Celta lo presente como defensa. Y de momento ha participado en las seis jornadas disputadas en la Hypermotion, contribuyendo a un decimoquinto puesto que, con mucho por jugarse aún, mantiene a los de Fredi Álvarez alejados del peligro. Roger, mientras, contempla orgulloso la evolución de su hijo. ‘Voltarei’, dice la canción del Celta. Y volvieron. Los Milla volvieron.

articles.title: Alarma en Las Palmas con una defensa en cuadro para Ipurua
articles.standfirst: De la Barrera sólo dispone de tres zagueros ante el Eibar y no sabe si puede contar con Álex Suárez
articles.summary: De la Barrera sólo dispone de tres zagueros ante el Eibar y no sabe si puede contar con Álex Suárez
articles.body: Las Palmas afronta el próximo partido con un serio problema en defensa. En ese escenario, Rubén de la Barrera solo tendría disponibles a tres futbolistas para ocupar las posiciones defensivas: Pezzolesi, Bonfanti y Andrés. Cruza los dedos el gallego para que Álex Suárez -en el final de recuperación- pueda sumarse a esa convocatoria. Y es que Enrique Clemente, lesionado de la rodilla, estará alrededor de mes y medio fuera. También por lesión son baja Marvin, Viti y Opoku, que ni siquiera ha podido debutar. Además, Herzog se encuentra concentrado con la selección española Sub-21. Una situación que deja a la plantilla al límite y obliga al cuerpo técnico a buscar soluciones de emergencia. La situación también pone el foco sobre la planificación de la dirección deportiva. Las salidas de Mika Mármol y Barcia dejaron dos huecos en el centro de la defensa que el club no cubrió con centrales de un perfil rápido. Esa carencia que quedó especialmente expuesta ante el Burgos, que encontró espacios a la espalda de la zaga en las acciones de sus dos goles. Un problema que no tiene fácil solución, ya que De la Barrera ha probado esta semana con Bonfanti y Andrés como la pareja en el centro de la zaga. A ello se suma la ausencia de un lateral izquierdo natural después de las salidas de Christian y Villote. Clemente asumió ese puesto, pero su lesión deja ahora al equipo sin un recambio específico. Loiodice jugó ahí ante el Burgos y repetirá en esa posición ante el Eibar, aunque el técnico dejó claro que, a pesar de que su posición natural no es la de lateral, es el perfil que mejor se adapta a lo que quiere. Otra muestra más de la descompensación existente en esa línea. El jugdor del filial Rachid acudirá a la cita, aunque esperará su oportunidad desde el banquillo.

articles.title: H-D, Chateaugay, P-H win boys soccer games
articles.summary: NAC soccer has been a season of one goal games in the boys West Division. The trend continued Wednesday as Hermon-DeKalb outscored Morristown 3-2 in boys’ ac...
articles.body:
NAC soccer has been a season of one goal games in the boys West Division. The trend continued Wednesday as Hermon-DeKalb outscored Morristown 3-2 in boys' action.

In NAC East boys action, Chateaugay shaded Madrid-Waddington 2-1 and Parishville-Hopkinton blanked Colton-Pierrepont 5-0.

H-D 3 - MCS 2: The Green Demons took leads of 1-0 and 3-1 in securing a win in a match of 2-1-1 teams.

"This division is going to go right down to the end. All of our games but one have been one goal games and I think that its going to be like that the whole season across the division," said Morristown Coach Jake VanArnam. "Today we didn't have our regular goalie and we had a midfielder get sick 10 minutes into the game and never return. They we had three players who couldn't play the second half because previous commitment. But Ayden Mitchell did a good job in net and we had some young guys playing unfamiliar roles step up and help us stay in the game."

Ethan Foster opened the scoring for H-D knocking home the ball in a scramble off a throw-in.

Owen Moore countered late in the first half by directing a low shot just inside the left goalpost. Ashtyn Smith scored early the second half for the Green Demons unassisted and Khristoffe Sy finished a Micha Walrath setup for a 3-1 lead.

Wyatt Clement revised Morristown's cause by netting a penalty shot. Hunter Bouchey made nine saves for H-D with a penalty shot stop and Mitchell finished with eight stops for MCS.

Chateaugay 2 - M-W 1: The Bulldogs broke a 1-1 tie with 16 minutes to play on a long throw-in after the Chateaugay goalie held firm in the face of sustained M-W offensive pressure. The Yellow Jackets gained a 1-1 tie five minutes before halftime when Zach Gilson finished a rebound opportunity from Kolby Todd.

"The second half was deadlocked with each team having scoring chances. We had two opportunities to punch in a second goal but the Chateaugay goalie held strong. Now we need to bounce back against Lisbon," said M-W Coach Quinn Shoen.

articles.title: JJ Gabriel: Barcelona sporting director denies interest in Manchester United teenager
articles.summary: Barcelona sporting director Deco says the club is not interested in Manchester United teenager JJ Gabriel.
articles.body:
Barcelona's sporting director Deco said the club has no interest in pursuing Manchester United teenager JJ Gabriel.

Gabriel, 15, travelled to the Spanish city after informing United that he wanted to leave Old Trafford earlier this month.

Real Madrid, Bayern Munich and Paris St-Germain are among the clubs reportedly keen on securing his signature.

"There's nothing to say about this boy," Deco said at a news conference.

"It's normal we always have players linked with us. There's a huge market for that, even when they are young.

"We are not interested in any player in his situation. I'm not sure what's happening, and if he's still a Manchester United player. We are not involved in that.

"First of all, we need to understand how the situation is before we try to do something. To speak about young, teenage players, it is not our business."

Gabriel has not trained at United since scoring a hat-trick on his Uefa Youth League debut on 10 September.

Tournament rules prevent him from playing for a side other than United in this season's competition.

But if he obtains a European Union passport through either his father - a former Republic of Ireland international - or mother, who has Greek-Cypriot heritage, he could join a club in the EU when he turns 16 on 6 October.

Last week, United manager Michael Carrick urged for people to be "careful and sensible" about the amount of exposure and scrutiny given to the youngster.

articles.title: Republic of Ireland vs Israel: 'Don't put pressure on us' over Israel games - Chiedozie Ogbene
articles.summary: Republic of Ireland winger Chiedozie Ogbene urges the public to not "put the pressure on us" over the campaign to boycott the upcoming Nations League games against Israel.
articles.body:
Republic of Ireland winger Chiedozie Ogbene has urged the public to not "put the pressure on us" over the campaign to boycott the upcoming Nations League games against Israel.

The sides are due to meet in Debrecen, Hungary on Sunday before the return fixture in Backa Topola, Serbia on 4 October (both 19:45 BST).

Since the sides were drawn together in Group B3, there has been increasing calls in Ireland to withdraw from the games due to the ongoing situation in Gaza with a 'Stop The Game' campaign gathering pace.

In the lead up to Thursday's 1-0 defeat by Kosovo in Pristina stand-in captain Dara O'Shea confirmed the players would meet on Friday to discuss their approach to Sunday's 'home' game for Israel, which will have no Irish fans in attendance before their behind-closed-doors match the following week.

"I'm aware of the feelings towards it," Ogbene told RTE Sport after Thursday's loss.

"It's a complicated and very difficult task. I just want to say and I hope people don't put the pressure on us to be answering difficult situations.

"There are people who can make the decisions and you can't rely on footballers to make those decisions. That's my feeling on it but as a group we will look at it and will see what we're going to do."

Republic of Ireland deservedly beaten by Kosovo

Neutral venues and no 'away' fans - how Israel v Republic of Ireland became so contentious

The armed Palestinian group Hamas attacked Israel on 7 October 2023, killing about 1,200 people and taking 251 hostages.

In response, Israel launched a massive military offensive in Gaza, during which more than 73,000 people have been killed, according to the territory's Hamas-run health ministry, whose figures are considered reliable by the United Nations (UN).

While the upcoming Israel games dominated discourse in the build-up to the Kosovo defeat, Ogbene does not accept that was a reason for a disappointing display in Pristina.

"I know there is a lot of discussion about things like that, but we just tried to focus on Kosovo today," said Ogbene.

"All our mindset was on Kosovo to win this game and then deal with that's coming."

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side had just two chances throughout the game with goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher making some fine saves, while Kosovo efforts were cleared off the line before the hosts finally broke the deadlock seven minutes from time through Vedat Muriqi.

It is yet another slow start to a Nations League campaign for the Irish and Ogbene accepts "it wasn't good enough", while also disappointed he was off-target with a big opportunity in the opening half.

"I thought we may have had enough quality to see it out at 0-0, but overall, it was poor from myself and poor from the standards we set ourselves," he reflected.

"I need to do more. I tried to focus on the ball and just mishit it, but I need to do better.

"We're overly disappointed with the result but most of all the performance as it's not like us."

articles.title: Uefa fears impact of Premier League spending in transfer market
articles.summary: Uefa believes "a clear two-speed system" is emerging in the transfer market due to huge spending by Premier League clubs this summer.
articles.body:
Uefa believes "a clear two-speed system" is emerging in the transfer market as a result of the huge spending by Premier League clubs this summer.

In its latest European club talent and competition landscape report, European football's governing body laid bare just how dominant the transfer activity of English clubs has become.

Uefa's report said that the estimated €4.6bn (£4bn) spend by Premier League clubs is "larger than that of the next eight largest European countries combined".

Andrea Traverso, Uefa's executive director of finance, said that this trend "raises concerns".

"Transfer values continue to rise sharply, particularly in the English market, increasing future pressure on club financial results," Traverso wrote.

"These developments also point to an increasing concentration of talent and a growing polarisation of the market, with the emergence of a clear two-speed system.

"English clubs were involved in more than 60% of the deals and paid an average of around €24m (£20.7m) per inbound player, compared with only around €4m (£3.4m) to €5m (£4.3m) in the other major European leagues, underlining a widening gap in purchasing power."

Traverso said that any "correction in transfer values" or "slowdown in buyer demand" could have serious implications for any club carrying debt.

The report added that the transfer spend of the 20 Premier League clubs this year is "equivalent to 56% of their annual revenue" - much higher than the 33% average of the pre-Covid decade.

Uefa also highlighted the increasing trend for English clubs to do big-value transfers between each other, which showed a 44% increase to €1.55bn (£1.33bn).

The English domestic market was "as large in fee value as the next five market flows combined".

A market flow describes league-to-league deals. After the English domestic market, the next most lucrative was the German Bundesliga to the Premier League, at €690m (£594m).

The number of European transfer fees paid above €50m has significantly increased, from 14 in the summer of 2024 to 23 in 2025. In 2026 there was another jump to 35 such deals, of which Premier League clubs were responsible for 29.

With pressure to pass financial regulations, clubs have increasingly looked to sell academy players as they provide pure profit on the books.

European clubs generated an estimated profit of €6.8bn (£5.85bn) on these sales over the summer, an increase of €655m (£564bn) on 2025.

Uefa also found little evidence of clubs using multi-club ownership structures to move players for inflated or reduced fees.

Total transfer fees of such deals were €152m (£130.8m) with an estimated market value of €159m (£136.8m).

More than half of this spend came from transfers between Chelsea and Strasbourg.

articles.title: Man Utd borrow another £90m to take debt to more than £1.1bn
articles.summary: Manchester United confirm they have borrowed another £90m since 30 June, to take their overall debt to more than £1.1bn.
articles.body:
Manchester United have borrowed another £90m since 30 June - and confirmed they spent £191.7m on new players this summer.

United bought Andrey Santos from Chelsea on 13 July, Youri Tielemans from Aston Villa on 14 July and Carlos Baleba from Brighton on 25 August.

The fees the club stated they spent on the trio at the time the transfers were announced added up to £153m, and it is not clear where the additional sum has been spent.

The club have been approached for comment.

Confirmation of the additional borrowing of £90m was included in a more detailed filing to the New York Stock Exchange on Thursday, following Wednesday's release of their 2025-26 accounts to 30 June, and showed their overall debt was still more than £1bn despite major cost-cutting measures implemented by Sir Jim Ratcliffe since he became minority owner in 2024.

United confirmed it made three further drawdowns from its revolving credit limit, on 29 and 31 July and 28 August, totalling £120m. It then paid back £30m on 21 September.

It takes United's overall debt to £1.15bn, made up of the historic debt, which now stands at £578m, the £200m outstanding on its revolving credit facility, and £375m in outstanding transfer fees.

That is a £72m reduction on the £447m they stated was owed in transfer fees in the 2024-25 accounts. However, it remains a large sum, with £104.8m due in between one and two years and £51.9m in between two and five years - with the remainder due in the next 12 months.

The club say payments for their most recent transfers "are due within the next five years".

articles.title: Portugal 1-0 Wales: Craig Bellamy wants more from his side after narrow Portugal loss
articles.summary: Craig Bellamy believes there is "more to come" from his Wales side in the Nations League following their opening-match loss in Lisbon.
articles.body:
Wales earned plaudits but Craig Bellamy wants more from his side, after admitting they were forced to suffer in their narrow 1-0 defeat in Portugal.

Joao Felix's deflected strike proved enough to earn victory in Lisbon for the hosts, who also saw Cristiano Ronaldo's effort ruled out by VAR.

It was a winning start to the Nations League title defence for Portugal and for new manager Jorge Jesus.

Despite being under pressure for long spells in Lisbon, Bellamy's injury-hit side ended strongly as Brennan Johnson and Lewis Koumas both went close to snatching a draw.

"It was a difficult game for us. We had to suffer a lot," said Bellamy.

"I think that's the longest we've been in a game without the ball.

"We could have done more with the ball but I'm beyond proud as well.

"We have a lot of players who weren't here. That's OK, we can handle it.

"A lot of players who don't play, week-in, week-out. So for them to use the energy they were able to, we've got to have a big heart to be able to do that. They've always shown that and they showed that again."

Felix strike earns Portugal narrow win over Wales

When Bellamy watched on as Ronaldo caused lockdown

Wales have a short turnaround to their second League A fixture against Denmark in Copenhagen on Sunday (17:00 BST).

But Bellamy feels his squad - missing Harry Wilson, Karl Darlow, Dylan Lawlor, Joe Rodon and Nathan Broadhead through injury - are capable of improving.

"There's more for us, so that's something we always look at as a positive," he said.

"How can we improve? How can we get better?"

Ronaldo unsurprisingly took the spotlight in the build-up to the contest at Jose Alvalade Stadium - where the 41-year-old began his professional career with Sporting in 2002.

The forward missed a big opportunity and had a goal disallowed for offside, which would have been his 980th top-flight goal, before being substituted midway through the second half.

He could well line-up against Wales again when Portugal play the return match in Cardiff in November.

Amid the noise around the Al-Nassr frontman, Bellamy refused to be overawed and hopes to face Ronaldo again.

"If you looked at everything that was going on, it's a £1.4bn squad you're up against, [but] I felt quite calm. The players give me that," added the Wales boss.

"Ronaldo is one of the greatest players of all generations, not just this generation.

"You have to plan for him because he's beyond dangerous, even at his age.

"He's a superstar and I'd love to think I'd have the opportunity to be up against him again, but I don't know, maybe time is ticking."

articles.title: Netherlands 1-1 Germany: Jurgen Klopp's first game in charge ends all square after late Cody Gakpo equaliser
articles.summary: Report from the UEFA Nations League Group A2 match between the Netherlands and Germany in Amsterdam; Felix Nmecha put the visitors in front, but Cody Gakpo's 92nd-minute equaliser prevented a perfect start for Jurgen Klopp
articles.body:
Former Liverpool manager Klopp took charge in July after their surprise early exit from the World Cup against Paraguay in the last 32 under Julian Nagelsmann.

His side appeared set to give him the perfect start after Felix Nmecha put Germany ahead, but Gakpo finished off a swift counter-attack in the closing stages to level the contest.

The result also gave Xavi Hernandez something to celebrate in his first game in charge of the Netherlands. He was appointed in August after Ronald Koeman stepped down following the Dutch side's elimination at the same stage of the World Cup.

Germany suffered an early blow when Jamal Musiala was ruled out before kick-off, after experiencing muscle pain - and they were given a scare when Virgil van Dijk headed in from a corner inside the first 15 minutes.

The goal was ruled out following a VAR review, however, with the Netherlands captain adjudged to have fouled Germany goalkeeper Marc-Andre ter Stegen.

Klopp's side were hit by another injury in the 30th minute when Arsenal's Kai Havertz was forced off, but they took the lead just two minutes later.

Philipp Treu's cutback found Nmecha, who made no mistake from close range to put Germany ahead.

The Netherlands had an injury concern of their own to contend with soon after, with Sunderland's Brian Brobbey taken off with what appeared to be a hamstring injury.

Germany almost doubled their advantage before half-time when Karim Adeyemi somehow failed to find the target from inside the six-yard box.

The Netherlands increased the pressure after the break and created a succession of chances, with Ter Stegen producing several important saves to preserve his side's lead.

Germany eventually succumbed in the closing stages, though, as Gakpo's late volley completed the Netherlands' comeback and secured an opening point.

Haaland brace fires Norway to winning start

Erling Haaland scored twice as Norway beat Denmark 3-2 in their UEFA Nations League Group A4 fixture in Oslo.

Fulham's Oscar Bobb put Norway in front after 14 minutes and Haaland made it 2-0 on 18 minutes.

Brentford's Mikkel Damsgaard, however, halved the deficit with a stunning free-kick and former Man Utd striker Rasmus Hojlund struck on the hour to level it at 2-2.

But Haaland struck with 16 minutes of the 90 remaining to seal the win, taking his tally to 64 senior international goals in just 56 appearances.

articles.title: Zidane quiere recuperar al Mbappé del que se "enamoró"
articles.standfirst: ‘Zizou’ reconoció que “le gusta mucho por izquierda” y desde Francia apuntan que empezará a utilizar a Kylian tirado a banda
articles.summary: ‘Zizou’ reconoció que “le gusta mucho por izquierda” y desde Francia apuntan que empezará a utilizar a Kylian tirado a banda
articles.body: Han pasado cerca de 2000 días desde que Zinédine Zidane dirigió un partido por última vez. Ha tenido tiempo, quizás demasiado, para proyectar lo que quiere hacer a los mandos de la selección francesa tras recoger el testigo de Didier Deschamps. Lo que está claro, tal y como apuntan en Francia, es que quiere recuperar la versión original de Kylian Mbappé. La primera prueba será contra Turquía en el estreno de la Nations League y, aunque se ausentó del primer entrenamiento por gripe, será de la partida. Fueron varias las ocasiones en las que se dio la oportunidad de que coincidiesen en el Real Madrid. Tanto en la primera, como en la segunda etapa de Zidane. Su relación, sin embargo, viene de mucho más atrás… y quedó constatado cuando ‘Zizou’ ejerció como ‘cicerone’ de Kylian en su presentación con el Real Madrid. “Lo conozco desde hace mucho tiempo y estoy enamorado. Vino aquí a una prueba hace mucho tiempo”, contó Zidane en 2019 en la previa de un Real Madrid-PSG de fase de grupos de la Champions. Aquella noche en el Bernabéu, con Icardi como referencia, Mbappé ‘se salió’ arrancando desde izquierda: completó 2/3 regates, repartió dos pases clave y fue el autor del 2-2 en los últimos minutos. Para los más escépticos, también recuperó cinco balones. El propio Kylian, tiempo después, reveló cómo inició esta relación con Zidane en The Players Tribune. “Que me llamara fue como estar en la luna”. Ocurrió en 2012, cuando tenía 13-14 años, y fue a entrenar con el Real Madrid en Valdebebas… tal y como se vio en las imágenes reveladas en el video de su presentación. Fue, de hecho, quién lo recogió en el parking del aeropuerto y lo llevó en su coche a la ciudad deportiva. Zidane, claro, fue preguntado por aquel episodio en la previa del partido contra Turquía: "Lo que vi en él fue su potencial cuando vino a hacer la prueba en el Real Madrid. Todos estábamos entusiasmados con la idea de verlo jugar aquí. No sucedió... pero ya conocemos el resto de la historia". De aquello han pasado casi 15 años y, por fin, ambos van a coincidir como técnico y jugador. “Bienvenido a tu casa”, escribió Mbappé tras el anuncio como seleccionador de Francia de un Zinédine Zidane que tiene claro que “es el mejor jugador del mundo” en su primera comparecencia ante los medios tras anunciar la convocatoria para el inicio de la Nations League. Zidane, además de asegurar seguirá siendo su capitán, destacó la versatilidad de Mbappé para desarrollarse por todo el frente de ataque. Sin embargo, destacó que le gusta “mucho por la izquierda” y, desde Francia, apuntan a que la idea que barrunta es ubicarlo como extremo a pie cambiado dentro de un 1-4-3-3 donde, como en su día hizo con Cristiano Ronaldo en el Real Madrid, gozará de plena libertad para acabar jugadas como segundo delantero. Mbappé viene de convertirse en el máximo goleador en la historia de los Mundiales tras anotar una decena de goles actuando como delantero. Un rol que comenzó a ejercer a partir de la Eurocopa 2024, cuando ni Kolo Muani ni Marcus Thuram lograron ocupar el vacío dejado por un Olivier Giroud que se retiraría de la selección tras aquel torneo. “He jugado tres Mundiales: uno por la derecha, otro por la izquierda y, de momento en este, como delantero. Eso demuestra que la posición en la que juego no es importante”, declaró Mbappé durante la pasada Copa del Mundo después de las críticas recibidas por un Didier Deschamps que tiró de ironía ante esta situación. “Debo ser estúpido por ponerlo de delantero centro… Lleva tres años jugando en una posición más centrada”. Mbappé, aunque en algún momento de su carrera se ha mostrado reacio a tener que desenvolverse como punta, reconoció que ha “progresado en algunos aspectos” y ha empezado “a aclimatarse al puesto”. Sus números, en banda (49% goles generados) o como referencia (51%), son prácticamente calcados con Francia. Zidane, sin embargo, tiene muy vivo el recuerdo de que sus mejores actuaciones —con la final del Mundial 2022 como mayor ejemplo— han llegado partiendo desde el costado y, al menos de primeras, va a intentar recuperar la versión de la que se "enamoró".

articles.title: Xavi: "Fuimos mejores que Alemania"
articles.standfirst: El técnico español se mostró muy satisfecho por el juego en su estreno con Países Bajos
articles.summary: El técnico español se mostró muy satisfecho por el juego en su estreno con Países Bajos
articles.body: Xavi Hernández se mostró "satisfecho" con el juego de Países Bajos en su estreno como seleccionador, en especial en una segunda mitad en la que, defendió, los neerlandeses mostraron "la personalidad" y la "ambición" que él quiere implantar a los jugadores. "Estoy satisfecho porque jugamos muy bien. Creo que, sinceramente, fuimos mejores que Alemania", aseguró Xavi en una rueda de prensa tras el encuentro disputado en el Johan Cruyff Arena de Ámsterdam, en el que los neerlandeses rescataron un empate 1-1 ante Alemania en el inicio de la Liga de Naciones. Alemania se adelantó en la primera mitad y Países Bajos tuvo que esperar hasta el tiempo añadido para encontrar el empate, con un gol de Cody Gakpo asistido por Ruben van Bommel. El exentrenador del Barcelona reconoció que a sus jugadores les costó situarse durante los primeros 45 minutos, algo que atribuyó en parte al comienzo de una nueva etapa. "En la primera parte quizá estuvimos un poco nerviosos, pero la manera en la que jugamos en la segunda parte es la correcta", explicó. Xavi destacó sobre todo la respuesta de su equipo después del descanso, cuando se encontraba por detrás en el marcador. "Mostramos personalidad, ambición, deseo de ganar y una buena intensidad", señaló el técnico. Además, añadió: "Lo que más me gustó fue, definitivamente, la personalidad en la segunda parte cuando íbamos perdiendo, la actitud de los jugadores y la mentalidad". El técnico español subrayó también la voluntad de dominar el balón como elementos del "nuevo" equipo neerlandés. "Presionamos arriba, recuperamos el balón y tomamos la iniciativa", explicó Xavi, para quien lo mostrado después del descanso debe convertirse en una referencia para el equipo: "Ese es el camino" y "ese tiene que ser el estándar" del equipo neerlandés, aseguró. El entrenador también afirmó no estar sorprendido por la forma de juego de los neerlandeses y subrayó haber visto ya durante los entrenamientos señales de la actitud de sus futbolistas. "Esto ya lo habíamos mostrado en los entrenamientos. Y como entrenas, juegas", afirmó. El empate abre una nueva etapa para Países Bajos después de su eliminación en el Mundial de 2026 en un partido ante Marruecos, a lo que siguió la salida de Ronald Koeman como seleccionador. Países Bajos disputará su próximo encuentro el domingo frente a la selección serbia.

articles.title: Turkiye vs France: UEFA Nations League – teams, kickoff time, lineups
articles.summary: Zinedine Zidane brings ‘aura’ to his first France game as coach, against Turkiye in Nations League.
articles.body:
Who: Turkiye vs France What: UEFA Nations League Where: Kocaeli Stadium in Izmit, Turkiye When: Friday, September 25, at 9:45pm (18:45 GMT) How to follow: Al Jazeera Sport will have all the build-up from 15:45 GMT.

Zinedine Zidane was asked if taking charge of his first France game on Friday will feel just as special as his playing debut for Les Bleus more than 30 years ago.

“Even more so, maybe,” a smiling Zidane said on Thursday ahead of a Nations League game in Turkiye. “I feel an immense emotion being at the head of this France team.”

Zidane’s dream was realised when he replaced Didier Deschamps after the 2026 World Cup. His former teammate Deschamps was in charge for 14 years, winning the World Cup in 2018 and losing the 2022 final.

Now it’s Zidane’s chance to make his mark on a team he once starred for.

Affectionately nicknamed “Zizou”, his face was beamed onto the Arc de Triomphe in Paris the night France celebrated its first World Cup triumph in 1998.

Zidane scored two headers in the final in a 3-0 win over Brazil and later that year he won the Ballon d’Or. Two years later, he was instrumental in France winning the European Championship.

His rise to the top seemed almost fated, for his international career began brilliantly in 1994 with two stunning goals against the Czech Republic after coming on as a substitute.

He then won league titles with Juventus and Real Madrid and scored a brilliant volley to help Madrid win the Champions League in 2002.

Zidane understands expectations are high, given his achievements as a player and how he led Real Madrid to three straight Champions League titles as a coach.

“It’s something new. I’m taking over as head coach so people are talking about it,” he said. “That makes sense.”

After facing Turkiye, France plays Belgium away on Monday before hosting Italy on October 2, and Belgium three days later, with both those games at the Stade de France.

Mbappe given all clear for France’s trip to Turkiye

France’s all-time top scorer Kylian Mbappe is set to captain the side, having shrugged off a minor injury.

Zidane was asked why, given that Mbappe is captain, he was not present at Thursday’s pre-match news conference. Instead, it was midfielder Adrien Rabiot who spoke to the media.

“The obligation is to have one player and the coach,” Zidane said. “[Mbappe] is fine. He will be ready to play tomorrow.”

Rabiot is one of France’s vice-captains along with forward Ousmane Dembele and right back Jules Kounde.

Rabiot said the huge attention placed on Zidane gave the players a welcome back seat.

“His aura means he commands a lot of attention,” Rabiot said. “In a way, it’s a good thing that the focus is more on the coach than the players. It gives them a bit more peace and quiet.”

Zidane understands the limelight but does not seek it.

“You have to accept how things are. But I’m not here for that,” he said. “Winning matches is what interests me the most.”

What happened the last time Turkiye played France?

The sides shared a 1-1 draw in Paris in 2019 in a qualifier for Euro 2020.

Olivier Giroud gave the home side the lead in the 76th minute before Kaan Ayhan levelled for Turkiye five minutes later.

This will be the seventh meeting between the nations, with France claiming four wins to Turkiye’s one in the previous encounters.

Turkiye will be without the services of Hakan Calhanoglu and Kenan Yildiz due to injury. Real Madrid starlet Arda Guler, however, is available despite fears of a knock.

Cakir; Celik, Demiral, Bardakci, Elmali; Ozcan, Kokcu, Yuksek; Guler, Yilmaz, Akturkoglu

Zidane can choose from six new faces in his squad.

Striker Esteban Lepaul (Rennes), defenders Leny Yoro (Manchester United) and Jeremy Jacquet (Liverpool), midfielder Lucas Da Cunha (Como), Andy Diouf (Inter Milan) and Guillaume Restes (Toulouse) are set for their debuts.

“I’m happy with what I’ve seen so far. The French team is open to everyone,” Zidane said. “We’ve got a good squad, some veterans, some newcomers.”

articles.title: Informe UEFA: La Premier gana por goleada: la que más gasta de largo y la que más público atrae a las gradas
articles.standfirst: Los entrenadores españoles son los más solicitados
articles.summary: Los estadios
articles.body: La UEFA ha emitido su informe anual sobre el impacto de este deporte entre los clubes europeos: la asistencia a los partidos, las tendencias y gastos en los fichajes o la utilización de los jugadores y los entrenadores en más de 700 clubes de las federaciones nacionales del máximo organismo europeo. El gasto de los clubes europeos en fichajes estivales, que superó por primera vez la barrera de los 5.000 millones de euros en 2017, ha rebasado la barrera de los 10.000 millones de euros por primera vez. Las ventas por traspasos de los clubes europeos, por valor de 10.300 millones de euros, han generado 6.800 millones de euros en beneficios netos que se incluirán en las cuentas de pérdidas y ganancias de los clubes correspondientes a los ejercicios 2026 y/o 2027. El poder económico del fútbol inglés está fuera de toda duda. El 52 % del valor total de los traspasos a nivel mundial involucró a al menos un club inglés. Su mercado interno creció casi 700 millones de euros y fue mayor que todos los demás mercados internos combinados. Las operaciones entre dos clubes ingleses generaron 2.200 millones de euros en concepto de traspasos. Solo los clubes ingleses recién ascendidos gastaron unos 545 millones de euros este verano, lo que representa el 71 % del gasto total de todos los clubes ascendidos. Ocho de los mayores flujos de traspasos involucraron a clubes ingleses, siendo los mercados nacionales alemán e italiano las únicas excepciones. Aparte del mercado nacional inglés, el flujo de traspasos de clubes franceses a ingleses fue, con diferencia, el mayor (algo menos de 800 millones de euros). Este verano se registró una fuerte representación de jugadores que militan en clubes europeos en la Copa Mundial de la FIFA. De los 1.248 jugadores presentes en la Copa Mundial Masculina de la FIFA 2026, el 68 % jugaba en clubes pertenecientes a federaciones miembro de la UEFA, y el 44 % lo hacía en clubes de las cinco grandes ligas europeas. Los clubes ingleses fueron los que contaron con mayor representación, aportando 204 jugadores (16 %). Los entrenadores españoles son los más demandados, con 74 de ellos trabajando en el extranjero en otros clubes europeos de primera o segunda división, por delante de italianos y croatas. Hubo 738 cambios de entrenador en la temporada 2025/26, lo que supone un aumento del 3 % en las destituciones de entrenadores principales en la temporada 2025/26 en comparación con la 2024/25. El 68 % de los entrenadores principales tuvieron carreras en el fútbol profesional. La rotación de entrenadores vuelve a superar la cifra de uno por club y temporada. Los despidos aumentaron a 738, con un promedio de 1,01 cambios por club de la máxima categoría. Se ha batido otro récord de asistencia, con al menos 242 millones de aficionados que asistieron a partidos de clubes y selecciones nacionales en Europa durante la temporada 2025/26. De nuevo aquí la Premier sale primera. En la temporada 2025/26, un total de 19 clubes registraron una asistencia a sus partidos de liga en casa superior al millón de espectadores: seis clubes en Inglaterra, cinco en Alemania, tres en Italia, tres en España y uno en Francia y otro en Escocia. Los clubes de primera división de Inglaterra, Alemania y los Países Bajos muestran una gran constancia en el apoyo de la afición, con una ocupación media superior al 90 % durante los partidos de liga nacional. Si bien ocho clubes llenaron al máximo el aforo de sus estadios durante los partidos de liga nacional, al menos 163 clubes de primera división registraron una ocupación del 70 % o más.

articles.title: Curt Cignetti Reveals Headset Issues During Indiana's CFP Title Win vs. Miami
articles.summary: Headset communications during Texas and Tennessee's Saturday matchup could potentially be impacted by President Donald Trump's plans to attend the game.
articles.body:
Headset communications during Texas and Tennessee's Saturday matchup could potentially be impacted by President Donald Trump's plans to attend the game.

Indiana coach Curt Cignetti told ESPN's Pete Thamel Thursday he experienced headset issues during January's national championship game, which Texas coach Steve Sarkisian previously said coincided with Trump's exit from the game.

According to Thamel, Cignetti said Indiana lost headset communications with around 6:45 left in the game and went without them at the end of a Miami touchdown drive.

"It came back before kickoff. We both had communication from that point on," Cignetti told Thamel.

Cignetti said the outage lasted long enough to encompass the play on which Miami's Malachi Toney caught a 22-yard touchdown pass, but that he was able to hear again after Indiana got the ball back, per Thamel.

Miami had one more offensive drive after that, during which the Hurricanes' hopes of a comeback were erased by Carson Beck throwing an interception with 44 seconds remaining.

Sarkisian told the Longhorn Network (h/t CBS Sports ) Miami had experienced headset disruptions in the fourth quarter, although he said the incident took place on the Hurricanes' final drive.

"The one thing that you have to be aware of is, when the president goes to any game, is that any time he enters the stadium or leaves the stadium or changes locations within the stadium, they cut off communication," Sarkisian said on the Longhorn Network . "So, they cut your headsets. They cut headsets to coaches. They cut headsets to coach-to-play communication, so you have to have a plan if, and or when. You get no warning. That just gets cut out.

"So, you have to have a plan for that... If comes in middle of the first quarter, or leaves in the fourth quarter, or decides he's got to use the restroom: Whatever that looks like, you've got to be prepared to have no comms for a short amount of time."

The White House confirmed to The Athletic's Ira Gorawara that Trump is planning to attend Saturday's game in Knoxville.

This will not be Sarkisian's first time involved in a game with Trump in attendance. He was serving as Alabama's offensive coordinator when Trump attended a 2019 game between Alabama and LSU.

Trump has also attended national championship games between Alabama and Georgia in 2018 and LSU and Clemson in 2020, as well as a regular-season matchup between Alabama and Georgia in 2024. He left each of those games early, per Adam Sparks of the Knoxville News Sentinel.

Saturday's matchup will pit two top-15 teams against one another in No. 1 Texas, where Arch Manning is looking to improve on last season's road struggles, and No. 14 Tennessee, where Faizon Brandon opened this season as the program's first true freshman starting quarterback since 2004. Kickoff is scheduled for noon this Saturday at Neyland Stadium.

articles.title: Why Broncos 2025 first-round pick getting reps on defense? Vance Joseph explains
articles.summary: The Denver Broncos face a challenging assignment in Week 3 when they host the Los Angeles Rams in Sunday night football. While the Rams were beaten badly in...
articles.body:
The Denver Broncos face a challenging assignment in Week 3 when they host the Los Angeles Rams in Sunday night football. While the Rams were beaten badly in the season-opening game against the San Francisco 49ers , Sean McVay's team responded well to that defeat with a one-sided triumph in Week 2 over the New York Giants .

Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford threw four TD passes in that game, and Denver defensive coordinator Vance Joseph knows that his secondary will be under the gun to be at its best against the team that most believe is the favorite to win this year's Super Bowl.

One of the players who is likely to see action in this game is nickel back Jahdae Barron . He did not make much of a contribution in Week 2 in the team's win over the Jacksonville Jaguars , but that may not be the case against the Rams. Joseph was asked about Barron — a 2025 first-round draft pick — and the coach said he is prepared on every play .

This is Barron's second year with the Broncos . He played in all 17 regular-season games a year ago and had 35 tackles, 5 passes defensed and 1 interception. The 5-11, 200-pound defensive back from Texas had 4 tackles in the season opener against the Chiefs , but he did not make any measurable contributions against the Jaguars.

The Broncos will be tested by Davante Adams , who had a 2-touchdown performance in the win over the Giants. Cornerbacks Patrick Surtain and Riley Moss will be tested by the Rams passing game, and that will be a more significant issue than slowing down the Jacksonville passing game.

articles.title: Week 3 Start 'Em, Sit 'Em Fantasy Running Backs
articles.summary: Welcome back, readers!
articles.body:
Welcome back, readers! I am happy to return for a second year as The Sporting Tribune's fantasy football analyst. If you are new here, my mission is to help fantasy managers with any dilemmas or questions they may have through the course of the season to ultimately win their leagues. For the next 17 weeks, I will produce weekly fantasy content that will go over the waiver wire, rankings, and Start 'Em, Sit 'Em columns.

Being a fantasy manager often means having to make difficult roster decisions, but I aim to take some of the guesswork out of it with my Start 'Em and Sit 'Em column for every position. It goes without saying that I won't include obvious calls like "start Trey McBride" or "sit Tommy DeVito." Instead, I search for players that could be perceived as fringe that could propel your lineups for weekly wins.

As always, if you have any questions or don't see your players here, feel free to follow me on Twitter (X) – @JamesNewell96 and send me a message, where I typically respond in a timely manner.

David Montgomery @ IND (Projected FPTS - 13.3): Montgomery had a dud performance and received fewer touches than backup Woody Marks, 13-8, in Week Two. He has a strong chance to bounce back in Week Three on the road against the Colts. Indy's defense has allowed the third-most fantasy points to running backs and is bottom three in success rate (51.5%), yards before contact per carry (3.5) and explosive runs (10). If I were to do an anytime touchdown parlay, I would have Montgomery on that slip.

D'Andre Swift vs. PHI (Projected FPTS - 13.9): Swift has had a compelling start to the season with 45.3 fantasy points, ranking as the RB5 in fantasy. And with Kyle Monangai putting up respectable performances, Swift has still touched the ball more than his backup, 36 percent to 21.6 percent. The Bears will likely be without their quarterback Caleb Williams in Week Three, which will result in a gameplan that leans more toward Swift (and Monangai).

Omarion Hampton @ BUF (Projected FPTS - 14.8): Omarion Hampton has been the only player on the Chargers to have any sort of fantasy relevance through the first two weeks. Despite the costly fumble against the Raiders last week, he still put up 115 yards and scored a touchdown on 25 touches. The second-year RB will take on the Bills in Week Three, who've allowed the fifth-most fantasy points and points per game to opposing running backs. Their struggle defending the run has been an ongoing concern since last season and hasn't improved much up to this point.

Honorable Mentions: Breece Hall @ DET; Chuba Hubbard @ CLE; Cam Skattebo vs. TEN; Kyle Monangai vs. PHI; TreVeyon Henderson @ JAX; Jaylen Warren vs. CIN.

Quinshon Judkins vs. CAR (Projected FPTS - 12.1): I believe this is a make-or-break week for Judkins. Through no fault of his own, the second-year RB is stuck behind a bad o-line paired with a poor offense, and he's averaged 2.3 yards per carry. Judkins has a good matchup on paper this week against the Panthers, but keep in mind that the numbers are inflated after the Bears' 59-point game in Week One, where both Bears RBs had monster games. I would wait to see what Judkins does this week before inserting him into lineups.

Jeremiyah Love @ SF (Projected FPTS - 12.4): Love has not seen RB1 usage so far this season. He ended up scoring just 7.5 fantasy points last week against the Seahawks. He gets another tough matchup in Week Three against the Niners, who are an above-average defense. Until the Cardinals start including him more in their gameplan on a weekly basis, I will likely lean toward benching the dynamic rookie.

Travis Etienne Jr. vs. LV (Projected FPTS - 12.1): What Etienne managers feared the most has officially happened. In Week Two, Alvin Kamara returned to the field and took away most of the extra usage Etienne saw in Week One. After seven receptions during the opening week, he only had two catches to Kamara's six in Week Two. His rushing ability hasn't lived up to expectations either, posting just 71 yards on 17 carries through two weeks. Kamara also led all Saints backs in touches at nearly 26 percent, which dropped Etienne's share to 18.5 percent, compared to Week One where he had 26.7 percent. This is not a good look for Etienne or Kamara, as this is turning into a three-back committee with undrafted rookie CJ Donaldson entering the fold. Etienne takes on the Raiders in Week Three, who've allowed the lowest EPA per rush after two weeks.

articles.title: Steve Sarkisian alleges Donald Trump altered 2026 CFP title game communications
articles.summary: Arch Manning and Texas could deal with similar issues against Tennessee in Week 4.
articles.body:
The 2026 College Football Playoff title game came down to the wire and Texas football 's coach claims Donald Trump had a role in the outcome.

Fernando Mendoza and the Indiana Hoosiers claimed their first national championship in school history after defeating the Miami Hurricanes , 27-21. However, January's title game may have been affected by the American president's attendance.

Steve Sarkisian will have to deal with the logistics of Trump reportedly being present at Week 4's college football showdown between the Longhorns and Tennessee Volunteers . Outkick's Clay Travis reported Wednesday the 80-year-old will be in Knoxville for the game on Saturday .

In the lead up to the game, Sarkisian dropped an interesting tidbit about what teams have to go through when the president is around. That includes an allegation that Trump may have altered key drives during the 2026 CFP finale.

How did Trump affect the college football game?

President of the United States Donald Trump attends UFC 327 at Kaseya Center. Mandatory Credit: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

Trump's no stranger to sporting events after frequenting UFC fights and even appearing at the 2026 FIFA World Cup final. However, Sarkisian says he was told by Miami coach Mario Cristobal that last season's CFP championship game had some intense moments after losing communication during the fourth quarter.

"A good friend of mine is Mario Cristobal," Sarkisian told the Longhorn Network . "Last year, when they were playing Indiana in the national championship, they had that drive at the end of the game; they had no communications because he was leaving early before the game ended. You get no warning; it just cuts out. You have to be prepared for that."

Several reports back up Sarkisian's claims, including that Trump's movement late in the game altered team communications. However, CBS Sports reveals that it was "only a play or two" and didn't "notably impact the outcome."

There's been some speculation that Trump would be on College GameDay in Week 4. That rumor's cooled since Johnny Knoxville was named guest picker for the ESPN pregame show.

Regardless, Heisman hopeful Arch Manning and Texas need to be prepared for any similar disruptions against Tennessee. It's unclear how long Trump will be in attendance at Neyland Stadium, but it's something to watch.

The Longhorns and Volunteers meet in Knoxville on Saturday (12 p.m. ET on ABC) with both SEC teams 3-0 entering the matchup.

articles.title: Nike fixed Kentucky Football up with some new heating and vibrating Hyperslides
articles.summary: Following the big road upset, the Kentucky football team will recover in the best way possible
articles.body:
Getting a road win at Kyle Field over the Aggies is a good enough gift to last a while, and this week, the Kentucky Football team received a special gift from Nike.

On Wednesday morning, Kentucky released a video of strength coach Brandon Roberts giving the guys the new Nike Air Zoom Hyperslides, a pair of shoes that, from afar, look like your everyday sandals or slides. They are far from a regular pair of those, though. These are recovery shoes that Nike says will "help reduce tension and promote relaxation."

In the video, you will notice a magnetic pod that controls heat and vibration in the shoes, with three levels of each for the wearer to choose from. The strap on top of the slides has a flap that opens and closes to provide easy access for the wearer. You can select the level you want at any time by tapping the pod or using the app. The slides can also be worn casually without the pod in.

Roberts also noted that Will Stein is the reason behind all of this. With Stein's relationship with Nike dating back to his days at Oregon, he just reached out to hook the guys up with some sweet new recovery slides.

"Appreciate you all for this. Coach Stein was able to get this, Nike, the Hyperice collab with these things. Nike, we appreciate what you all do for us."

The players responded, "Appreciate you, Nike!"

It may be hard for us fans to lace up the cleats and go upset a top-10 in the country, but at least we can recover like them! If you would like to get your own pair, it'll cost you $249. They come out on September 29 on nike.com , hyperice.com, and at select retail locations.

articles.title: Week 3 Start 'Em, Sit 'Em Fantasy Wide Receivers
articles.summary: Welcome back, readers!
articles.body:
Welcome back, readers! I am happy to return for a second year as The Sporting Tribune's fantasy football analyst. If you are new here, my mission is to help fantasy managers with any dilemmas or questions they may have through the course of the season to ultimately win their leagues. For the next 17 weeks, I will produce weekly fantasy content that will go over the waiver wire, rankings, and Start 'Em, Sit 'Em columns.

Being a fantasy manager often means having to make difficult roster decisions, but I aim to take some of the guesswork out of it with my Start 'Em and Sit 'Em column for every position. It goes without saying that I won't include obvious calls like "start Trey McBride" or "sit Tommy DeVito." Instead, I search for players that could be perceived as fringe that could propel your lineups for weekly wins.

As always, if you have any questions or don't see your players here, feel free to follow me on Twitter (X) – @JamesNewell96 and send me a message, where I typically respond in a timely manner.

Drake London @ GB (Projected FPTS - 15.3): Historically, London isn't usually a name you'd expect in this column, but his recent dip in fantasy production has earned himself a spot on this list. By no fault of his own, his performances could be boosted with an efficient QB under center. In Week Three he should have that with Michael Penix Jr. returning as the starter, which should aid London against Green Bay's beatable secondary. Expect the USC product to have a bounce-back week.

Jalen Coker @ CLE (Projected FPTS - 13.3): It's only been two weeks, but Coker has proved to be the real deal. In both games, he has recorded eight catches on nine targets, and only four receivers have more receiving yards (204) and fantasy points (48.4) than Coker. He has more targets than the NFC's defending Rookie of the Year and fellow Panther Tetairoa McMillan. He is a must-start this week against the Browns, who allowed the seventh-most fantasy points to the position.

Malik Nabers vs. TEN (Projected FPTS - 14.6): It is safe to assume that fantasy managers are a little worried about Nabers, who had an ugly 1.1 fantasy point performance and missed some time during the game with a shoulder injury in Week Two. I can't bury the lead here, but now his quarterback Jaxson Dart will be out for the remainder of the season. However, I still believe in the talent and the significant role he has in this system. He has a favorable matchup this week against the Titans defense, who let Garrett Wilson and DeVonta Smith have impactful weeks. With a week's worth of game planning with Jameis Winston under center, expect Winston to target Nabers often.

Honorable Mentions: DeVonta Smith @ CHI; Ladd McConkey @ BUF; Denzel Boston vs. CAR; Devaughn Vele vs. LV; Deebo Samuel Sr. @ MIA; Christian Watson vs. ATL; Parker Washington vs. NE.

Luther Burden III vs. PHI (Projected FPTS - 11.0): Throughout the offseason, one of the most targeted and praised players I had was Burden. But the first two weeks of the season have not looked reassuring. He's combined for 15.7 fantasy points, and fellow Bears wideout Kalif Raymond has received more targets. Also, the Bears will be without their quarterback Caleb Williams after he sustained a hamstring injury in Week Two. I am not giving up on the second-year receiver, but I am hesitant to start him until he either puts up a commendable performance on the field or Williams returns under center. This week he takes on the Eagles, who are no slouch in the secondary. He's a risk-or-reward type player in Week Three.

Marvin Harrison Jr. vs. SF (Projected FPTS - 9.6): I listed Harrison as a sit last week, and he will be again this week against the Niners. In Week Two against the Seahawks, he finished with a goose egg after only being targeted one time. In two games, he's only had four targets… FOUR. Both Michael Wilson and Kendrick Bourne have more targets than the former fourth-overall pick from two years ago. I don't expect him to do anything in another tough divisional matchup. Two things will happen if Harrison has another stinker this week. One, fantasy managers should not only keep Harrison exclusively on the bench, but they should consider releasing him. Two, I might not feature him on this column anymore, because he's shown nothing but disheartening performances and has become too easy of a name to mention on this list. It might sound extreme or harsh, but it's the truth.

Terry McLaurin vs. SEA (Projected FPTS - 11.1): I was expecting more out of McLaurin last week against the Cowboys. He has recorded a pair of dud performances to open the season, and I would be worried to put him in your lineups this week against the Seahawks. The Commanders will have veteran quarterback Marcus Mariota as their starter after Jayden Daniels suffered a dislocated elbow right before halftime in Week Two. Even with Mariota's experience, the Seahawks' stout defense has allowed the fewest fantasy points, yards, touchdowns, and points per game to wide receivers.

Lowlights: Courtland Sutton vs. LAR; Chris Godwin Jr. vs. MIN; Carnell Tate @ NYG; Brian Thomas Jr. vs. NE; DK Metcalf vs. CIN; Jameson Williams vs. NYJ; Josh Downs vs. HOU.

articles.title: "La culpa para los periodistas, pero no hace falta rebajar cada elogio con siete advertencias: Noval es una joya"
articles.summary: La opinión de Nacho Labarga
articles.body: A Benja Noval no hay que meterlo en una urna. Ni envolverlo en plástico de burbujas. Ni convertir cada conversación sobre su futuro en un interminable “tranquilidad, tranquilidad, tranquilidad”. Tiene 17 años, sí. Y precisamente por eso lo mejor que puede hacer el ciclismo español es dejarle correr. Porque hay algo casi absurdo en nuestra manera de gestionar el talento. Cuando aparece uno distinto, primero exigimos que gane. Y cuando gana demasiado pronto, nos entra miedo de que siga ganando. Pedimos paciencia como si la ambición fuese una enfermedad y la presión una maldición. Noval acaba de conquistar dos Mundiales en 48 horas y todavía parece que haya que pedir perdón por decirlo alto: este chico es extraordinario. No significa proclamar que será el nuevo Contador, el nuevo Evenepoel o el nuevo Pogacar. Esa manía de buscar reencarnaciones también sobra. Noval debe ser Noval. Pero tampoco hace falta rebajar cada elogio con siete advertencias. Sus victorias obligan a mirar de frente lo evidente. Montreal ha enseñado a un corredor capaz de soportar el cartel de favorito, asumir la carrera, atacar cuando todos le miran y rematar. Eso no se aprende en un laboratorio. Se tiene o no se tiene. Y él, además, no parece asustado. Dice que le gusta la presión. Mejor. Bendito problema. La presión que nace de ganar es infinitamente preferible a la indiferencia que acompaña a tantos proyectos que nunca terminan de arrancar. Ahora llegará el discurso de siempre: quemar etapas, protegerle, no correr demasiado, no exigir resultados. Todo razonable hasta que la protección se convierte en freno. A los grandes talentos hay que cuidarlos, claro. Pero cuidar no consiste en atarlos. Si Noval tiene piernas para competir con los mejores, que compita. Si puede ganar, que gane. Si algún día explota, que aprenda. Si pierde, que pierda. El ciclismo también se construye así. España llevaba demasiado tiempo esperando a alguien capaz de provocar este ruido. Ahora que ha aparecido, lo peor que podría hacer sería pedirle que bajase la voz. Que nadie le coloque todavía una corona que no le corresponde. Pero que tampoco le corten las alas por miedo a que vuele demasiado alto. Benja ya ha demostrado que saber ganar cuando todos esperan que gane. Y eso no se protege escondiéndolo. Toca aprovecharlo. Menuda joya.

articles.title: Informe UEFA que retrata la realidad del fútbol femenino en Europa: 5,1 millones de espectadores
articles.standfirst: "Panorama del talento y las competiciones en los clubes europeos"
articles.summary: "Panorama del talento y las competiciones en los clubes europeos"
articles.body: La cifra de asistencia a los partidos femeninos en Europa durante la temporada 2025/2026 alcanzó los 5,1 millones de espectadores, según el informe anual de la UEFA "Panorama del talento y las competiciones en los clubes europeos" publicado este viernes. El estudio, que analiza las cifras de asistencia, el talento de las jugadoras y los entrenadores, además de las estructuras de las competiciones femeninas, destaca el aumento presencial de aficionados y el crecimiento del fútbol femenino europeo. Detalla que 3,7 millones de espectadores acudieron a los partidos de máxima categoría en la campaña 2025/2026, cifra que aumenta a 5,1 millones si se incluyen la Liga de Campeones femenina, los partidos de categorías inferiores y las copas nacionales. El informe de la UEFA ha analizado también la participación de las jugadoras en 15 ligas de máxima categoría, seleccionadas en función de una combinación de factores: el mercado nacional, los coeficientes de clubes y federaciones de la UEFA, el coeficiente de la FIFA y la disponibilidad de datos. Entre sus datos, concluye que de media en 2025/26 los equipos alinearon un total de 4.400 jugadoras y que se alcanzó un récord de 386 participantes en la fase liga de la Liga de Campeones -un aumento del 14 % con respecto a la temporada anterior-. El de 2025/26 fue el segundo ejercicio en el que se exigió a los clubes inscribir al menos ocho jugadoras formadas localmente en sus plantillas de 25. Estas representaron el 48 % del total de minutos jugados durante la fase liga de la temporada 2025/26 -un 3 % más que la previa-. El documento destaca que más de la mitad de los clubes (52 %) de las cinco grandes ligas no realizaron cambios en el cuerpo técnico durante la temporada y que el 63 % de los entrenadores y entrenadoras principales de las cinco grandes ligas poseía una licencia UEFA Pro la última campaña. España lidera la clasificación con un 89 %. El porcentaje de clubes integrados en estructuras existentes ha aumentado del 43 % en 2020 al 59 % en la presente 2026/27. En consonancia con esto, el 27 % de los clubes de la máxima categoría femenina operan de forma independiente de los masculinos, lo que supone una disminución de más del 10 % en relación a hace cinco años. "El tamaño y los formatos del fútbol femenino nacional siguen evolucionando", remarca la UEFA, que apunta que 52 de sus 55 federaciones nacionales cuentan con una liga de máxima categoría, que van desde Kazajstán, con 19 equipos, hasta Armenia y Gibraltar, con cuatro equipos.

articles.title: Álvaro Cervera y el 'reino' de las dos aficiones
articles.standfirst: El técnico con más partidos en el banquillo del Tenerife recibe este sábado en el Heliodoro a un Cádiz con el que también ostenta ese récord
articles.summary: El técnico con más partidos en el banquillo del Tenerife recibe este sábado en el Heliodoro a un Cádiz con el que también ostenta ese récord
articles.body: Este sábado será un día más que especial para Álvaro Cervera. El técnico que más partidos ha dirigido en la historia del Tenerife (180) y Cádiz (257) será el gran protagonista de una cita que reunirá a los dos clubes de su vida en los banquillos. Nadie en la historia moderna de Segunda ha logrado ceñirse aún esa doble corona como entrenador. Su impronta, caracterizada por el orden defensivo, el contragolpe y el esfuerzo global, es el rasgo más reconocible de la propuesta futbolística que desarrolló en esas dos orillas atlánticas. Cervera es el puente invisible que une el Heliodoro y el Carranza, dos aficiones que le profesan agradecimiento y pleitesía casi por igual, y que también están hermanadas por otros vínculos que forman parte de su particular idiosincrasia como el carnaval. Cervera ha entrelazado para siempre al Cádiz y al Tenerife. Llegó cuando los equipos atravesaban por una situación crítica en lo deportivo y, tras instaurar una identidad propia, logró los ascensos que devolvieron la felicidad a unas hinchadas que habían sido castigadas en los años previos a su pizarra por unas prestaciones inferiores a la historia de ambas entidades. Su manual de supervivencia es ya toda una garantía para amarillos y blanquiazules. Tras superar las críticas iniciales, su estilo terminó siendo religión para unas aficiones rendidas al rendimiento que es capaz de extraer en sus futbolistas. El Heliodoro reunirá este sábado a dos equipos que, en el corazón de la mayoría de sus seguidores, comparten el mismo soberano en su banquillo. Pocos son capaces de sobrevivir en entornos tan exigentes como los de Tenerife o Cádiz. Cervera lo consiguió con creces y, por esa razón, el reino de su credo futbolístico se extiende hoy por igual entre blanquiazules y amarillos

articles.title: Konaté cae en la 'maldición de los centrales' del Madrid
articles.standfirst: Los contratiempos físicos se han cebado con esa posición en las tres últimas temporadas: 35 lesiones y 1.701 días de baja
articles.summary: Los contratiempos físicos se han cebado con esa posición en las tres últimas temporadas: 35 lesiones y 1.701 días de baja
articles.body: Ahora Konaté. El Madrid estrenaba nuevo central en la plantilla y en un mes de competición ya lo tiene en la enfermería, tras lesionarse con la selección. El defensa regresa a Madrid con un leve esguince en la rodilla derecha. No parece un contratiempo físico especialmente serio, pero lo que sí preocupa al club es que el fantasma de la 'maldición de los centrales' vuelve a sobrevolar por Valdebebas. Precisamente Konaté llegó en verano para reforzar un centro de la defensa debilitado por las lesiones. Alaba no renovó tras vivir un calvario, Militao no iba a poder arrancar la temporada y Rüdiger necesita 'cuidados', pese a que su retirada de la selección es una tregua clave para aliviar el castigado físico. Están siendo años en los que el Real Madrid ha sufrido una plaga de lesiones en el centro de la defensa que lo ha tenido en jaque en muchas ocasiones. Por ese motivo apareció Asencio desde el Castilla, se exprimió a Tchoauaméni como central y la posición se ha visto reforzada en los dos últimos mercados de verano con las llegadas de Huijsen y Konaté. Pero la 'maldición' parece no dar tregua en este comienzo de la temporada y la baja de Konaté es una prueba de ello. Es más, de las ocho lesiones que ha sufrido el Madrid de Mou hasta el momento, la mitad han afectado a los centrales: dos de Asencio, una de Huijsen y la última de Konaté. Llueve sobre mojada y el Madrid se echa a temblar con los precedentes, que resultan tremendamente inquietantes. Dos datos: 35 lesiones sufrieron los siete centrales que ha tenido el Madrid en su plantilla en las tres últimas temporadas, para un total de 1.701 días de baja entre todos ellos. Ahora, transcurrido sólo un me de la presente campaña, ya son tres los centrales que se han lesionado: Asencio, Huijsen y Konaté. El informe de las bajas en el centro de la defensa es demoledor. Militao es el caso más doloroso para el Madrid. El brasileño, llamado a liderar la zaga del Madrid tras las salidas de Ramos y Varane, no levanta cabeza: 8 lesiones, 700 día de baja y sólo 52 partidos disputados de un total de 179 en las tres últimas temporadas. La actual la ha empezado en la enfermería, recuperándose de la última lesión de larga duración que sufrió el pasado mes de abril. Alaba ya se fue, pero si no está en el Madrid es entre otras cosas porque las lesiones lo machacaron: 8 lesiones, 607 días de baja y 47 partidos jugados de 179 en las referidas tres últimas temporadas. Rüdiger aguantó como un titán las largas ausencias de sus dos compañeros en la zaga, pero se le llevó al límite y acabó cayendo. El alemán ha sufrido 5 lesiones, 195 días de baja y ha jugado 129 partidos de 179 en las tres últimas temporadas. La juventud de Huijsen y Asencio tampoco les ha librado de los bajas por problemas físicos. El primero, en su primer año, visitó la enfermería hasta en cinco ocasiones, siendo baja 69 días y jugando 40 partidos de los 56 de la pasada temporada. Asencio aguantó el tipo el año de su irrupción, pero ya la pasada temporada sufrió con la lesiones: 3 problemas físicos y 31 días de baja. Además, esta temporada la ha empezado acumulando 2 lesiones y 44 días de baja. La lista de centrales 'caídos' en las tres últimas temporadas la completan Nacho y Vallejo, fuera del Madrid hace más tiempo. El primero, en la 23-24, la última como madridista, acumuló 2 lesiones y 23 día de baja. El segundo, en la 24-25, sufrió 4 lesiones y estuvo 76 días fuera de combate. Ahora Konaté ha pasado a engrosar una lista que tantos quebraderos de cabeza le ha dado al Madrid en los últimos tiempos.
